header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Rajiv Kumar (CTO, HealthScale), Elena Morales (Head of Compliance, HealthScale), Sam Ortega (Cloud Architect, HealthScale), Priya Nair (SRE, HealthScale)
summary: POC scoping call to align on private networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency requirements, egress constraints, workload sizing, and benchmark success criteria. Customer (HealthScale) is evaluating Redwood Private for regulated PHI-adjacent workloads. Key outcomes: agreed to run benchmarks in us-east-1 with PrivateLink and VPC peering configs; customer to provide workload sample and IPs; Redwood to provide network diagram, security docs, and preliminary pricing.
topics: Network topology options: VPC Peering vs AWS PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway
Workload sizing: RPS, sequence lengths, concurrency
Benchmark plan: metrics (p99 latency, throughput, error rate, token cost)
Success criteria for POC and timelines
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off the POC scoping for the private networking piece. goal is to scope out VPC peering vs PrivateLink and confirm data residency for HealthScale.
[00:15] Rajiv (HealthScale): Thanks, yeah, we're evaluating a Private deployment because of compliance — we process PHI-adjacent telemetry and need audit logs, KMS control and region pinning.
[00:30] Jonas (Redwood): Totally get it. Quick intro from our side: I'm Jonas, SE, I run the benchmarking and network setup for Private. Lina will help on the security docs. Maya is your AE.
[00:45] Elena (HealthScale): Hi — my main concern is the egress paths. We have pretty strict rules, certain vendor endpoints get blocked. Also want assurance that logs and keys never leave our control.
[01:05] Lina (Redwood): On keys we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations, and we can show the audit log flow. For networking, there are two common patterns: VPC Peering (low latency but cross-account route tables) or AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) which is more controlled but introduces ENI IP considerations.
[01:30] Sam (HealthScale): Can you call out the differences in latency and ops? we care about p99 generation latency — our UX target is sub 500ms for sync completions on short prompts.
[01:50] Jonas: For small models and short seqs, peering tends to add negligible latency. PrivateLink adds a small extra hop but is usually within 10-30ms depending on region and path. The bigger variance is from instance sizing, batching, and cache warm state.
[02:10] Rajiv: Ok. Our initial traffic will be about 300 requests/minute peak, expected avg 512 tokens per request, spiky bursts up to ~800 rpm during clinic hours. We need to size for concurrency and token throughput.
[02:30] Maya: Great detail. For the POC we often ask customers to provide a representative sample load and a synthetic harness we can replay. That lets us measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and token cost.
[03:00] Sam: We'll try to provide that. Also, we operate primarily in us-east-1 with DR in eu-west-1. Data residency: primary data must remain in us-east-1; backups in eu-west-1 are ok but must be encrypted and accessible only to our keys.
[03:20] Lina: Redwood Private supports region pinning and private control plane options. For backups and logs we can configure retention and region controls. We'll flag the KMS/HSM integration path for you.
[03:45] Elena: SOC 2 evidence and any FedRAMP-ish controls? We have two auditors interested.
[04:00] Maya: We'll share SOC2 report and the security whitepaper after the call. For FedRAMP that's a longer conversation but we can map controls.
[04:15] Jonas: Back to networking — practical steps: we need the customer's VPC CIDR ranges, a list of allowed egress IP ranges, and whether you prefer PrivateLink or peering. If you have strict egress blocks, PrivateLink is often easier since we present an interface endpoint in your account. But note PrivateLink requires ENIs and IP allocations.
[04:45] Sam: We currently have an egress appliance that blocks everything except a small allowlist. We prefer not to open broad routes. PrivateLink sounds safer. Any limits on concurrent connections for PrivateLink?
[05:05] Jonas: No hard limit from Redwood at the infra level, but AWS ENIs scale with throughput, and there are connection scaling considerations that we test during the POC. We'll include guidance for scaling ENIs and cross-AZ setup.
[05:25] Rajiv: For benchmarking success criteria, what do you recommend we measure?
[05:35] Jonas: We propose: 1) P99 latency under target (you said <500ms for short prompts) for representative prompt set; 2) sustained throughput at your baseline (300 rpm) with <1% error rate; 3) cold and warm cache scenarios — prefix caching matters for stateful workloads; 4) throughput cost estimate (tokens/min cost) for given config; 5) security checklist verification (KMS, SAML/SSO, audit logs).
[06:05] Maya: Also decision criteria: if latency or egress constraints block PrivateLink and cost for Dedicated is within budget, you might opt for Dedicated + peering. We'll present both numbers.
[06:20] Elena: On data flow — does Redwood ever see plaintext content? We need assurance about at-rest encryption and in-flight encryption, and whether we can use our own KMS.
[06:35] Lina: You can use your KMS keys for model encryption at rest. In flight is TLS and PrivateLink keeps traffic within AWS network. We also support putting the control plane in your VPC for extra isolation.
[06:55] Priya (SRE): For routing: if we use peering, do we need to update route tables in multiple subnets? Our infra team wants a list of specific route/NACL changes.
[07:10] Jonas: Yes, we'll provide a diagram and the exact route/NACL/security group rules. We'll call out required ports (HTTPS 443, health checks). We'll also show Nat/GW considerations if your subnets are private.
[07:30] Rajiv: Timeline — how long to stand up a POC?
[07:40] Maya: Typical POC is 2-4 weeks. Week 0 (setup & network config), Week 1 (bench harness and dry run), Week 2 (full load and tuning), Week 3 optional for longer validation and handoff. For Private networking we aim for the shorter side if samples and network info are provided quickly.
[08:05] Sam: We'd like a strict timeline for legal & procurement too — we need the security addendum before infra work.
[08:20] Maya: We can provide the security addendum and SOC2 docs in two business days. Procurement signoff often runs in parallel with the POC.
[08:35] Elena: Also need RBAC: we want SCIM/SAML SSO and granular roles for engineers vs compliance auditors.
[08:50] Lina: Redwood supports SAML SSO and role-based access; audit logs can be exported to your log storage (S3/CloudWatch/ELK) within the pinned region. We'll add config notes.
[09:10] Rajiv: For benchmarks, what hardware are you using in Dedicated/private? GPU types?
[09:20] Jonas: Our Dedicated pools use A10G / H100 depending on model size; for smaller open models we run on A10G equivalent instances. We'll propose a config matching your latency/throughput needs. We'll include quantization recommendations if cost is a driver.
[09:40] Sam: For initial POC please match the open model X we plan to use (we'll share exact model name later). Also show fallback policies if a region is constrained.
[10:00] Jonas: Noted — provide model name and tokenization stats. We'll run both peering and PrivateLink paths and compare p99 latency and egress footprints.
[10:20] Priya: Are there any IP allowlist size limits for PrivateLink? our security wants to keep lists small.
[10:30] Jonas: PrivateLink uses interface endpoints allocated into subnets; you don't need a large allowlist — you allow the endpoint ENI addresses. We'll show the number of ENIs per AZ and approximate IP counts.
[10:50] Rajiv: Cost concerns — what's the incremental cost of PrivateLink vs peering?
[11:00] Maya: PrivateLink has additional AWS endpoint charges and possibly more egress; peering is free on AWS but can be complex cross-account. We'll provide cost estimates in the pricing doc.
[11:20] Elena: On retention and logs: we need the audit trail for model calls for 1 year and ability to redact certain fields for privacy.
[11:35] Lina: We can stream logs to your S3 with encryption and lifecycle. Redaction at rest is trickier — we'll discuss redaction in the evals and how to avoid storing sensitive fields.
[12:00] Sam: For the test harness, can Redwood run the replay from our sample in your env or do we run the harness into your endpoint?
[12:15] Jonas: We can do both. For PrivateLink we often ask customers to run the harness from inside their VPC pointing at the PrivateLink endpoint (most realistic). If you can't, we can run a replay from our test agents peered into your VPC with your permission.
[12:40] Rajiv: What success criteria would get us to the next phase?
[12:50] Maya: I'd say: 1) Technical: meet p99 latency target (<500ms) for the short prompt set and sustain baseline throughput with <1% errors; 2) Security: SOC2 docs provided, KMS integration validated, network config validated; 3) Cost: preliminary TCO within X% of your target (we'll define X in pricing doc); 4) Stakeholders sign-off.
[13:25] Elena: That sounds reasonable. Also want a runbook for incident scenarios and rollback if the model misbehaves.
[13:40] Lina: We'll include an ops runbook and can demo tracebacks and token-level cost breakdown in the console.
[14:00] Maya: Next logistics: Jonas will share the network diagram and bench plan; I'll share SOC2 and security addendum; customer will share workload sample and egress constraints.
[14:15] Sam: We'll try to get the sample and IPs by Friday. Procurement will review addendum first and then legal.
[14:30] Rajiv: Anything else on regions? We need confirmation that control plane can be pinned to us-east-1 and logs kept in eu-west-1 for DR.
[14:45] Lina: Control plane pinning is possible for Private deployments; logs/backup region rules we'll document.
[15:00] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with dates. Thanks everyone.
[15:10] Elena: Thanks.
[15:12] End of call
